title: Why The "10x Engineer" Is A Dangerous Myth
summary: Podcast clip: Dave Farley and guest agree 10x engineers exist but are a bad target; writing code is not the hard part, and self-styled 10x devs offload tech debt.

assertions.quote: I think the thing probably exists, but I think it's a dumb target

verdicts.note: Large individual variation is consistently observed, but the specific tenfold figure traces to small studies from the 1960s and 70s.

Interpersonal work time differences are real and larger than most experimental effects, but the slowest-to-fastest-quarter ratio is rarely above 4 and the Grant/Sackman 28:1 figure (really 14:1) looks like an outlier; the author cautions that student populations may understate practical variability.

Work-time bad/good ratios within a language ran 1.5 (C) to 3.2 (Perl), with three Java programmers at 40-63 hours against a 10-hour median; so a several-fold spread exists on one small task but not an order of magnitude in the typical case.

assertions.quote: not conscious of the tech debt that they were fluffing off onto everyone else

verdicts.note: Widely reported anecdotally; no study measures downstream debt created by high-output individuals.

assertions.quote: writing code is not the hard part. It never has been.

verdicts.note: Maintenance is generally estimated to consume well over half of lifecycle effort, though the exact figures are poorly sourced.

Relays Glass's view that understanding existing code is the dominant maintenance activity and a field study finding developers spend about 60% of their time on program comprehension; secondary citations, not measured in this study.
Introduction cites maintenance consuming over 70% of lifecycle cost and reading code being the most time-consuming maintenance activity; background citations rather than findings of this paper.
Opens by citing a field study that developers spend most of their time (70%) understanding code; a secondary citation used as motivation.

assertions.quote: there's room for lots of different definitions of excellence depending on what is needed by the team

verdicts.note: A values statement about what counts as excellence.
